additional_material_claims.source_excerpt: The ninth verse shows the basic denseness of the hypocrites - how they failed to make use of the ordinary sense of discrimination. They had grown up in a pagan society, and knew very well what the way of the infidels was. Now they had become familiar enough with Islam too, and could easily see the difference. But, in their greed, and for the sake of petty worldly profit, they still chose disbelief as against Islam, and bartered away something as invaluable as Iman ایمان (faith) for something as worthless, and even harmful as kufr کفر (infidelity). In giving the name of 'trade' or 'commerce' to this action, the Holy Qur'an suggests that these worldly-wise men had no understanding even of the art of trading.

additional_material_claims.source_excerpt:
The Example of the Hypocrites

Allah likened the hypocrites when they bought deviation with guidance, thus acquiring utter blindness, to the example of a person who started a fire. When the fire was lit, and illumnitated the surrounding area, the person benefited from it and felt safe. Then the fire was suddenly extinguished. Therefore, total darkness covered this person, and he became unable to see anything or find his way out of it. Further, this person could not hear or speak and became so blind that even if there were light, he would not be able to see. This is why he cannot return to the state that he was in before this happened to him. Such is the case with the hypocrites who preferred misguidance over guidance, deviation over righteousness. This parable indicates that the hypocrites first believed, then disbelieved, just as Allah stated in other parts of the Qur'an.

citations.proposition: The idols’ entry into the Fire demonstrates that they were never true gods.

citations.quoted_clause: a Fire whose fuel is people and stones, overseen by formidable and severe angels
citations.proposition: A warning to believers also describes the Fire as fuelled by people and stones.

transmitted_evidence.statement: Qatādah reads this as a lack of power to meet the challenge, while Ibn ʿAbbās says that any attempt will fail.
transmitted_evidence.proposition: Qatadah and Ibn Abbas affirm that challengers lack the power to succeed in producing the demanded likeness.
transmitted_evidence.source_excerpt:

transmitted_evidence.statement: Ibn ʿAbbās understood the stones as sulphur, which stresses the terror and heat of the fuel.
transmitted_evidence.proposition: Ibn Abbas interprets the stones as sulphur used among the Fire’s fuel.
transmitted_evidence.source_excerpt: (And if ye do it not-and you can never do it-) this you can never do and if you try you will never succeed (then guard yourselves against the Fire) if you are bent on not believing, for you should fear hell (whose fuel is men) the unbelievers, (and stones) of sulphur, (prepared) created, prepared and preordained (for disbelievers).
